title: Current architecture decision journeys — payment, service workflow and database migration
authority: Implementation-authored regression cases, not an independent held-out benchmark. They assess the current native records without reinstating retired implicit workload assumptions. Expert review and real provider responses are still needed for architectural quality conclusions.

bank-payment.description: The current illustrative bank payment reference: stable payment identity, one financial effect, durable handoff and uncertain settlement. No request workload is stated.

service-workflow.description: A retained teaching fixture with one service boundary, a transactional work record and a comparison with an independent worker. It carries illustrative wording, not measured production evidence.

mysql-migration.description: An authored existing-service scenario comparing retained MySQL with PostgreSQL. Migration requires a justified driver or capability gap and an owned conversion/rollback plan; product version and workload evidence are unknown.

cases.prompt: Distinguish accepting a payment instruction from completing settlement. Explain which drivers and unanswered facts determine synchronous completion or durable asynchronous acknowledgement.
Compare authoritative repeat protection with application cache suppression. Where must one financial effect be enforced, and what evidence remains required?
A settlement call timed out. Compare retrying with outcome enquiry and reconciliation without treating timeout as proof that no financial effect occurred.

Assess the posting and settlement contracts together. Identify required execution facts for durable delivery, repeated calls and authoritative outcome discovery; prose alone is not proof of execution behavior.
What can be concluded about the runtime capacity with no saved workload objective? Identify missing evidence without inventing a throughput target or replica count.

Compare the existing queue/log options against the required delivery, replay, ordering and ownership obligations. Preserve unknown configuration facts and distinguish product capability from verified system behavior.
Explain how the one-financial-effect driver constrains responsibilities, interfaces, technology configuration and tests. A target of zero duplicate effects is a requirement, not a measurement.
Compare a single owned service with an asynchronous worker. Identify which additional drivers would justify distributing this small workflow and which operating obligations that choice creates.
Assess repeat handling and visibility of processing outcomes. Identify what remains unknown before recommending a queue or retries.
Keep the teaching scenario's illustrative conditions separate from an agreed project capacity target. What measured workload and failure evidence would the architect need?

Does the supplied evidence justify replacing MySQL with PostgreSQL? Compare retaining the existing database with migration, identify missing version and workload facts, and preserve the migration constraint.

Does changing the database engine solve the workflow's repeat and outcome obligations? Separate transaction boundaries and application behavior from product selection, and identify the evidence required before changing this existing service.
